text: Cockerels are used for breeding from 6 months of age to ensure viable sperm. Cocks have no penis; mating happens by pressing the vent of the cock to the vent of the hen. A good ratio is one cock per 15 hens — too many cocks lowers fertility because they waste time fighting. The infundibulum also stores sperm, where fertilization takes place; the germinal disc, a small white spot on the yolk surface, is where sperm enters the egg. Near the junction of the vagina and uterus is a gland that can store sperm for 10 to 15 days — when an egg is laid, some stored sperm can be released and migrate up to fertilize another egg, a trait specific to birds where sperm stays viable at body temperature.
